title: Where Sahara Meets the Sea
titleFr: Là où le Sahara rejoint la mer
highlights: Hot-air balloon ride over the Agafay desert at sunrise
Private evening walk through Marrakech's Secret Gardens
Two-hour hike to the Cascades d'Akchour in the Rif Mountains
Exploration of Chefchaouen — Morocco's legendary Blue City
Guided visit to Hassan II Mosque built over the Atlantic Ocean
includes: Accommodation in selected riads and hotels with daily breakfast
Meals as listed in the programme
Private air-conditioned vehicle and driver throughout
English-speaking guide for all tours and transfers
Entrance fees to all sites listed in the programme
excludes: Beverages with meals and meals not listed in the programme
Optional activities (hot-air balloon, hammam, zipline, quad biking)
Personal expenses — laundry, phone calls, gratuities
whatsapp_message: Hi, I'm interested in the 9-day Morocco Grand Tour 'Where Sahara Meets the Sea'. Can you send me pricing and availability?
subtitle: A curated private passage through Morocco's four great cities — balloon rides at dawn, blue medinas at dusk, and the silence between.
heroAlt: Ornate Moroccan riad archway glowing with warm lantern light at dusk

itinerary.title: Arrival — The City Breathes You In
itinerary.desc: Arrive at Casablanca Mohammed V airport and transfer by private vehicle to Marrakech — a two-hour drive through olive groves and argan orchards. Check into Riad Palais Blanc in the medina. That evening, a private guided walk through the Secret Gardens and Dar el Bacha, then a slow wander into Jemaa el-Fna as the square comes alive.

itinerary.title: Palaces, Pigments & a Desert Dinner
itinerary.desc: Morning at Bahia Palace and a visit to a traditional apothecary. Then Majorelle Garden — the electric-blue sanctuary created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and rescued by Yves Saint Laurent. Optional lunch inside the garden and a visit to the Amazigh Museum. Late afternoon, the city gives way to the Agafay stony desert for a candlelit dinner under canvas.

itinerary.title: Sunrise from 1,000 Feet — The Balloon Day
itinerary.desc: An early-morning hot-air balloon flight over the Agafay desert and palm groves, with the Atlas Mountains glowing on the horizon. Champagne breakfast on landing. The remainder of the day is free for a hammam, a cooking class, or exploring the souks at your own pace.

itinerary.title: The Capital's Quiet Power
itinerary.desc: Drive north to Rabat, Morocco's understated royal capital. Visit the Chellah necropolis — a ruined Roman city absorbed by a medieval Islamic sanctuary where storks nest on broken minarets — then Hassan Tower and the Mausoleum of Mohammed V. Check into La Tour Hassan Palace. Evening at leisure.

itinerary.title: Kasbah by the Sea
itinerary.desc: A morning exploring Rabat's medina and Bab el-Had market before entering the Kasbah of the Udayas — a fortified village perched above the Bou Regreg estuary with Andalusian gardens overlooking the Atlantic. Optional pre-booked lunch. Free afternoon.

itinerary.title: The Blue City, Unveiled
itinerary.desc: Drive into the Rif Mountains to Chefchaouen, a medina painted in every shade of blue. Private guided walk through Ras el-Maa spring, the historic kasbah, the winding derb alleyways, and Place Uta el-Hammam as the evening call to prayer echoes off the mountain. Dinner and overnight at Dar Jasmine.

itinerary.title: The Waterfall at the End of the Trail
itinerary.desc: A two-hour guided hike through cedar forest and limestone gorges to the Cascades d'Akchour. Outdoor lunch by the water. Return to Chefchaouen in the afternoon for optional quad biking or a zipline ride over the valley. Overnight in Chefchaouen.

itinerary.title: The Mosque at the Edge of the Ocean
itinerary.desc: Drive along the Atlantic coast to Casablanca. Check into Radisson Blu. Guided visit to Hassan II Mosque — the third-largest mosque in the world, built partially over the sea, with a retractable roof and a 200-metre minaret. Free time to explore the Corniche and Art Deco quarter.

itinerary.title: Farewell — Until the Next Medina
itinerary.desc: Breakfast at the hotel. Private transfer to Mohammed V International Airport for your onward flight. End of services.

testimonials.quote: The balloon ride alone was worth the entire trip. But what I'll remember most is Chefchaouen at six in the morning, before any other tourists arrived.
testimonials.author: Layla M.

testimonials.quote: Our guide knew which door to knock on to find the best pastilla in the medina. That's the kind of detail money can't buy from a guidebook.
testimonials.author: Thomas R.

testimonials.quote: Nine days felt like a month in the best possible way. Rabat was the surprise — nobody talks about Rabat. They should.
testimonials.author: Amira K.
